item.title: “‘Māra, Māra,’ venerable sir, is said. What, venerable sir, is Māra?” - “Form, Rādha, is Māra. Feeling is Māra. Perception is Māra. Formations are Māra.…
item.description:
“‘Māra, Māra,’ venerable sir, is said. What, venerable sir, is Māra?” - “Form, Rādha, is Māra. Feeling is Māra. Perception is Māra. Formations are Māra. Consciousness is Māra. Seeing thus, Rādha, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form … with feeling … with perception … with formations … with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated. In liberation, knowledge arises: ‘Liberated.’ He knows: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 23.11

item.title: “Monks, as long as the community of monks is not dominated by craving — that craving which leads to another state of existence — then,…
item.description:
“Monks, as long as the community of monks is not dominated by craving — that craving which leads to another state of existence — then, monks, the community of monks can be expected to prosper and not decline.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 16 – Mahāparinibbānasutta

item.title: “Monks, wander in your own proper range, in your own ancestral territory. Monks, if you wander in your own proper range, in your own ancestral…
item.description:
“Monks, wander in your own proper range, in your own ancestral territory. Monks, if you wander in your own proper range, in your own ancestral territory, then longevity will increase, beauty will increase, ease will increase, wealth will increase, power will increase.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 26 – Cakkavattisutta

item.title: “Monks, these six sense bases — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — bring suffering. What six? The eye sense base, monks — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained…
item.description:
“Monks, these six sense bases — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — bring suffering. What six? The eye sense base, monks — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — brings suffering. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … The mind sense base, monks — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — brings suffering. These six sense bases, monks — unguarded, unprotected, unguarded, unrestrained — bring suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.94

item.title: “Monks, misconduct in sensual pleasures, when performed, developed, and cultivated, leads to hell, to the animal realm, to the realm of hungry ghosts. The very…
item.description:
“Monks, misconduct in sensual pleasures, when performed, developed, and cultivated, leads to hell, to the animal realm, to the realm of hungry ghosts. The very least result of misconduct in sensual pleasures is being born human with enmity from adversaries.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.40

item.title: “Monks, how does a monk practice the qualities befitting an ascetic? Here, monks, for a monk, when the mind of sensual desire exists, that sensual…
item.description:
“Monks, how does a monk practice the qualities befitting an ascetic? Here, monks, for a monk, when the mind of sensual desire exists, that sensual desire is abandoned; when the mind of ill-will exists, that ill-will is abandoned; when the mind of anger exists, that anger is abandoned; when the mind of hostility … hypocrisy … spite … envy … stinginess … deceit … fraud … obstinacy … impetuosity … conceit … arrogance … vanity … heedlessness exists, that heedlessness is abandoned … Monks, I say that if he practices the qualities befitting an ascetic, he can abandon the defilements that are stains of an ascetic, blemishes of an ascetic, faults of an ascetic, leading to a plane of misery, to a bad destination, to the taking up of an evil realm. He sees himself cleansed of all those evil, unwholesome states and sees himself liberated. Because he sees himself cleansed of all those evil, unwholesome states and sees himself liberated, gladness arises; from gladness, joy; from joy, the body becomes tranquil; from bodily tranquility, he experiences ease; from ease, the mind becomes concentrated. I say that it is because of inner mental concentration that he practices the qualities befitting an ascetic.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 40 – Cūḷa-Assapurasutta

item.title: “Monks, the bones of a single person, if collected and preserved without being destroyed, would form a heap of bones, a pile of bones, a…
item.description:
“Monks, the bones of a single person, if collected and preserved without being destroyed, would form a heap of bones, a pile of bones, a mass of bones as great as this Mount Vepulla.

The bones of a single person
Accumulated in one lifetime
Would be a heap like a mountain —
So said the Great Sage.

This great mountain of bones
Is called Vepulla,
North of Vulture’s Peak
In the Magadhan hills.

But one who sees the Four Noble Truths
With perfect wisdom —
Suffering and its origin,
The transcending of suffering,
The Noble Eightfold Path
Leading to suffering’s stilling —

That person, wandering at most
Seven more times,
Makes an end of suffering,
Destroying all fetters.”

From: Itivuttaka 24
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “One who avoids sensual desires As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head — That mindful one transcends This attachment in the world. Whoever is greedy…
item.description:
“One who avoids sensual desires
As one’s foot avoids a snake’s head —
That mindful one transcends
This attachment in the world.

Whoever is greedy for sensual pleasures —
Land, gold, cows, horses,
Servants, attendants, women, relatives —

Weak, overcome by sensual pleasures,
Calamity crushes him,
Suffering follows him
As water rushes into a broken boat.

Therefore, always mindful,
One should abandon sensual pleasures.
Having abandoned them, one crosses the flood,
Having bailed out the boat, one reaches the far shore.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 4.1
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, for direct knowledge of greed, six things should be developed. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception…
item.description:
“Monks, for direct knowledge of greed, six things should be developed. What six? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. For direct knowledge of greed, monks, these six things should be developed.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.142

item.title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise…
item.description:
“I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise attention. Through wise attention, monks, unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to full development.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.75
